trajectory_summary: Craig called with a narrow, already-decided need — remove and later reinstall his existing solar system during a renovation, no new sale desired — and stated this clearly five times. The rep, running the standard qualify-then-bill-swap-then-design script, never recognized this as a non-standard scenario requiring a different path, and the mismatch drove the customer from cooperative to confrontational to disengaged. The call ends with no appointment and no clear answer given to the customer's repeated, specific question.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Recognizing and routing non-standard requests (removal-only, no new sale)
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I mean, do do you guys I so I don't want I don't wanna have to go down on that route. I mean, do you guys just have the service to remove the panels?
primary_coaching_focus.why: Craig asked this exact direct question and never got a direct answer across three follow-up exchanges; the rep kept defaulting to the standard design/bill-swap script instead of pausing to confirm what Ion actually offers for a removal-only request, which drove the customer to disengage.

key_moments.quote: Is there any way on the title but you and your wife? Or sorry. Just you?
key_moments.stewart_read: Craig discloses he had a prior company (Fluent Solar) for the existing system. The rep never probes what happened with that company, why it ended, or whether it's relevant to the removal request — competitive/relationship context a closer or specialist would want.

key_moments.quote: Is she she looking into solar too?
key_moments.stewart_read: Mary Anne, the actual title-holder/homeowner, is not on the call. Instead of treating this as a co-owner-inclusion moment (schema requires the title co-owner be part of the appointment), the rep asks a generic interest question and drops it entirely once Craig says they already have panels. This is more consequential than a standard spouse-objection miss because Mary Anne owns the home outright and Craig is not even the titleholder.

key_moments.quote: Were you looking for, like, an add on?
key_moments.stewart_read: Craig's answer ('we need them removed and reinstalled until the home reno is finished') is a scenario orphaned_flow doesn't fully cover — it's not a lease/PPA DQ, not an 'add-on' interest, and not a broken-system case. It's a temporary removal-for-renovation request. The rep's one qualifying question here doesn't map onto any of orphaned_flow's four listed checks (own/lease, prior company, panel size, system working), and the rep never asks the one relevant orphaned_flow item that WOULD apply — whether the current system is working — before pivoting into the standard new-design pitch.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. Well so we have a program. It's called the the bill swap.
key_moments.stewart_read: Immediately after Craig explicitly says he isn't looking to buy panels, the rep launches into the full bill-swap pitch anyway — premature program-selling into a customer who has already signaled it doesn't apply to him.
